If you're considering Gentoo, you might want to try Sabayon first. You get all the same packages, but almost all of them are pre-compiled for you (which saves you a lot of time for Chrome, KDE, etc.), and you also get a default set of USE flags that makes the initial setup significantly easier. As an added bonus, the package managers (for both Gentoo and Sabayon) are extremely colourful, which makes their output much easier to read. The only downside is that you don't really want to change the configuration (USE flags, versions, etc.) for the core system packages that everything else depends on, because that can make updates kind of messy.

Arch you definitely don't want to upgrade without reading the news on their website first, or you can miss stuff like when they updated the default python symlink to point to Python 3 (guaranteed to break all kinds of things.)

tldr: Arch is if you want your system to break regularly, Gentoo is if you want to customize the USE flags for every little thing, and Sabayon is if you're too impatient to run Gentoo. :P
